docs.title: ProxyCraft
docs.text: ProxyCraft is a config-driven HTTP/HTTPS reverse proxy. Point it at a JSON file, run one command, and route traffic to remote APIs, package registries, or local files — with caching, filtering, and URL rewriting built in.

docs.title: What you can do
docs.text: Goal How ProxyCraft helps Mirror PyPI, npm, Maven, or Alpine packages on your network Ready-made registry endpoints with disk cache and URL rewriting Put a stable URL in front of a third-party API HTTPS reverse proxy with path-based routing Serve a fake API while a backend is not ready Mock backend with path templates and JSON responses Try local packages first, then fall back to a remote registry Virtual upstream with first-match strategy Block bots or unwanted client IPs IP and User-Agent filters with Ant-style patterns Speed up repeated GET requests Per-endpoint file cache with TTL and size limits

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
pip install proxycraft

Create proxy.json:

{
  "version": "1.0",
  "name": "My proxy",
  "endpoints": [
    {
      "prefix": "/",
      "match": "**/*",
      "backends": {
        "https": {
          "url": "https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts"
        }
      },
      "upstream": {
        "proxy": { "enabled": true }
      }
    }
  ]
}

Run it:

from proxycraft import ProxyCraft

ProxyCraft(config_file="proxy.json").serve(host="0.0.0.0", port=8091)

Requests to http://localhost:8091/1 are forwarded to the upstream API.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• MkDocs user documentation (features, use cases, configuration, deployment)
  • just docs-build and just docs-serve recipes; GitHub Actions workflow to build and publish docs
  • proxycraft/shared/utilities/http_compat.py shim for HTTPMethod on Python 3.10
  • proxycraft/shared/utilities/path_compat.py helper for Path.is_file(follow_symlinks=...) on Python 3.10 and 3.11
  • Feature-based package layout under proxycraft/features/, proxycraft/shared/, and proxycraft/app/
  • docs/architecture.md and ADR docs/decisions/0001-feature-based-architecture.md

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Supported Python versions expanded from 3.13+ to 3.10 through 3.14
  • Reorganized package from layer-based folders to features/, shared/, and app/
  • Moved logging, utilities, connection pooling, and async file reader into proxycraft/shared/
  • Moved configuration, routing, upstream backends, middleware, authentication, protocols, virtual upstream, and deployment into proxycraft/features/
  • Co-located unit tests beside feature and shared modules
  • Updated SPECS.md, README.md, and pytest.ini test discovery paths

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: ProxyCraft is entirely driven by a JSON config file. Each endpoint maps incoming URL paths to a backend and optional upstream options (proxy, cache, virtual sources).

docs.title: Top-level fields
docs.text: Field Description version Config schema version (use "1.0") name Human-readable proxy name timeout Default upstream timeout ssl Enable TLS on the proxy listener server ASGI server type, port, and certificate paths middlewares Global security and performance middleware endpoints List of routed paths and their backends

docs.title: Endpoint anatomy
docs.text:
Every endpoint needs at least a path match and a way to produce a response:

{
  "identifier": "my-api",
  "prefix": "/api",
  "match": "/api/**",
  "weight": 10,
  "backends": {
    "https": {
      "url": "https://api.example.com/v1"
    }
  },
  "upstream": {
    "proxy": { "enabled": true, "timeout_seconds": 60 }
  }
}
Field Purpose prefix URL prefix stripped before forwarding to the backend match Ant-style pattern that selects this endpoint (**, *, {id}) weight Higher weight wins when multiple endpoints match backends Handler that fulfills the request (HTTPS, mock, echo, …) upstream Proxy settings, per-endpoint cache, or virtual sources transformers Find/replace rules on response bodies

docs.title: Backend types
docs.text:
Type Use when https Forward to a remote HTTP/HTTPS service echo Return request metadata (debugging, health checks) mock Serve fixed JSON from path templates redirect HTTP redirect to another URL command Run a shell command and return stdout

See Backends for examples of each type.

docs.title: Global middleware
docs.text:
Apply security and performance rules to all endpoints:

{
  "middlewares": {
    "security": {
      "ip_filter": {
        "enabled": true,
        "blacklist": ["10.0.0.0/8"]
      },
      "bot_filter": {
        "enabled": true,
        "blacklist": [{ "name": "scraper", "user-agent": "*bot*" }]
      }
    },
    "performance": {
      "resource_filter": {
        "enabled": true,
        "skip_paths": ["favicon.ico", "robots.txt", ".well-known/**"]
      },
      "cache": {
        "file": {
          "enabled": true,
          "path": ".cache",
          "ttl": 86400,
          "max_size_mb": 1024
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

Per-endpoint cache and transformers override or extend these defaults. See Caching and Security filtering.

docs.title: Multiple HTTPS backends
docs.text:
List backends with weights for future load-balancing; today the first healthy backend is used:

"backends": [
  {
    "https": [
      { "id": "primary", "url": "https://pypi.org/simple", "weight": 10 },
      { "id": "mirror", "url": "https://mirror.example.com/simple", "weight": 5 }
    ]
  }
]

docs.title: Virtual upstream
docs.text:
Combine several endpoints into one URL — try sources in order until one returns HTTP 200:

{
  "prefix": "/packages",
  "match": "/packages/**",
  "upstream": {
    "virtual": {
      "sources": ["local-packages", "remote-packages"],
      "strategy": "first-match"
    }
  }
}

Source names refer to other endpoints' identifier fields. See Virtual upstream.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: ProxyCraft validates the config at startup. Fix typos in field names or missing required backend URLs before serving traffic.

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text: Run ProxyCraft on a laptop, in Docker, or behind a load balancer. Everything is controlled by your JSON config file.

docs.title: Run with Python
docs.text:
from proxycraft import ProxyCraft

ProxyCraft(config_file="/etc/proxycraft/proxy.json").serve(host="0.0.0.0", port=8080)

Or pass host and port in code; config server.port is used when serve() is called without arguments.

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
docker build -t proxycraft -f dockerfiles/proxycraft.Dockerfile .
docker run -d \
  -p 8080:8080 \
  -v /etc/proxycraft/proxy.json:/app/proxy.json:ro \
  -v /var/cache/proxycraft:/app/.cache \
  --name proxycraft \
  proxycraft

For registry mirrors, persist the cache volume. Mount your config read-only.

docs.title: ASGI servers
docs.text:
server.type Best for gunicorn Production Linux, multiple workers uvicorn Simple deployments, development hypercorn HTTP/2 and built-in TLS

Example:

{
  "server": {
    "type": "gunicorn",
    "port": 8080,
    "workers": 4
  }
}

docs.title: HTTPS
docs.text:
{
  "ssl": true,
  "server": {
    "type": "hypercorn",
    "port": 443,
    "certfile": "/etc/ssl/certs/proxycraft.pem",
    "keyfile": "/etc/ssl/private/proxycraft.key"
  }
}

Place TLS termination at ProxyCraft or at an external load balancer — both work. If the load balancer handles TLS, run ProxyCraft on HTTP internally.

docs.title: Production tips
docs.text:
• Config — keep proxy.json in version control; inject secrets via env or sidecar files if needed
  • Cache — use a dedicated disk for .cache/ on mirror instances
  • Security — enable IP filtering on internal-only mirrors
  • Timeouts — set timeout_seconds per endpoint for slow upstreams (registries, large artifacts)
  • Logging — ProxyCraft uses structured logs; forward stdout to your log aggregator

docs.title: Upgrade
docs.text:
pip install -U proxycraft

Review Changelog before upgrading in production.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pipuv 
pip install proxycraft

uv add proxycraft

docs.title: Run your first proxy
docs.text:
1. Create a config file proxy.json (see Configuration for the full schema).
  2. Start the server:
from proxycraft import ProxyCraft

if __name__ == "__main__":
    ProxyCraft(config_file="proxy.json").serve(host="0.0.0.0", port=8091)
  1. Send a request:
curl http://localhost:8091/

ProxyCraft loads defaults from its built-in template when fields are omitted. For a full working example with registry mirrors, mocks, and caches, copy proxycraft/features/configuration/default.json from the repository.

docs.title: Choose an ASGI server
docs.text:
Set the server in your config:

{
  "server": {
    "type": "gunicorn",
    "port": 8080
  }
}

Supported values: gunicorn (default), uvicorn, hypercorn.

docs.title: Enable HTTPS on the proxy
docs.text:
Terminate TLS at ProxyCraft by providing certificate paths:

{
  "ssl": true,
  "server": {
    "type": "hypercorn",
    "port": 8443,
    "certfile": "/path/to/cert.pem",
    "keyfile": "/path/to/key.pem"
  }
}

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
docker build -t proxycraft -f dockerfiles/proxycraft.Dockerfile .
docker run -p 8080:8080 -v $(pwd)/proxy.json:/app/proxy.json proxycraft

Mount your config and cache directories as volumes when running registry mirrors in production.

docs.title: Backends
docs.text: Each endpoint uses one backend handler to produce a response. Pick the handler that fits the job.

docs.title: HTTPS
docs.text:
Forward to a remote service. The most common backend.

"backends": {
  "https": {
    "url": "https://api.github.com",
    "ssl": true
  }
}

docs.title: Echo
docs.text:
Return request details — useful for debugging clients and load balancers.

"backends": {
  "echo": {
    "enabled": true,
    "add_headers": {
      "X-Echo-Service": "true"
    },
    "response_delay_ms": 100
  }
}

docs.title: Mock
docs.text:
Serve canned JSON without a real upstream. Ideal for frontend development and contract tests.

"backends": {
  "mock": {
    "enabled": true,
    "path_templates": {
      "/users": {
        "status_code": 200,
        "content_type": "application/json",
        "body": { "users": [{ "id": 1, "name": "Jane" }] }
      },
      "/users/{id}": {
        "status_code": 200,
        "body": { "id": "${path.id}", "name": "User ${path.id}" }
      }
    },
    "default_response": {
      "status_code": 404,
      "body": { "error": "Not found" }
    }
  }
}

See Mock API for development.

docs.title: Redirect
docs.text:
Send clients to another URL, optionally keeping the original path:

"backends": {
  "redirect": {
    "enabled": true,
    "location": "https://api.github.com",
    "preserve_path": true
  }
}

docs.title: Command
docs.text:
Run a shell command and return its output (platform-specific; use with care in production):

"backends": {
  "command": {
    "id": "diagnostics",
    "default": "echo ok"
  }
}

docs.title: Choosing a backend
docs.text: Need Backend Call a real HTTP API https Stub responses during development mock Verify what the client sent echo Move traffic to a new host redirect Run a one-off diagnostic script command

docs.title: Caching
docs.text: Speed up repeated GET requests by storing responses on disk. Caching is configured per endpoint or globally under middlewares.performance.cache.

docs.title: File cache
docs.text:
"upstream": {
  "proxy": { "enabled": true },
  "cache": {
    "file": {
      "enabled": true,
      "path": ".cache/pypi",
      "ttl": 43200,
      "max_size_mb": 256,
      "max_entries": 2500,
      "include_patterns": ["/pypi-remote/**"],
      "exclude_patterns": ["/health"]
    }
  }
}
Option Meaning ttl Seconds before a cached entry expires max_size_mb Maximum cache directory size max_entries Maximum number of cached responses include_patterns / exclude_patterns Limit which paths are cached

docs.title: Global cache defaults
docs.text: Set defaults once in middlewares.performance.cache.file and override per endpoint when needed. Registry mirror presets in the default config enable file caching for PyPI, npm, and Maven endpoints.

docs.title: Resource filter
docs.text:
Skip noisy paths so they never hit upstream or cache:

"resource_filter": {
  "enabled": true,
  "skip_paths": [
    "favicon.ico",
    "robots.txt",
    ".well-known/**"
  ]
}

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Air-gapped or slow networks — cache package index pages and artifacts after the first download
  • Rate-limited APIs — reduce calls to upstream providers
  • CI runners — share one on-prem mirror instead of pulling from the public internet on every build

Pair caching with response transformation on registry mirrors so cached HTML still points at your proxy URL.

docs.title: Response transformation
docs.text: Rewrite text inside upstream responses so clients see URLs that point back to your proxy instead of the original host.

docs.title: Text replacements
docs.text:
"transformers": {
  "response": {
    "enabled": true,
    "textReplacements": [
      {
        "oldvalue": "https://pypi.org/simple",
        "newvalue": "http://mirror.internal:8080/pypi-remote-official"
      },
      {
        "oldvalue": "/simple",
        "newvalue": "/pypi-remote-official"
      }
    ]
  }
}

Rules run in order. Each oldvalue is replaced with newvalue in the response body.

docs.title: Why it matters for mirrors
docs.text:
Package registries embed their own URLs in HTML index pages. Without rewriting, pip, npm, or Maven would follow links back to the public internet instead of your mirror.

Typical replacements:

Registry Replace PyPI https://pypi.org/simple → your mirror base URL npm https://registry.npmjs.org → your mirror base URL GitHub API https://api.github.com → your gateway path

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Package registry mirror — mandatory for PyPI simple index and npm metadata
  • API gateway — rewrite documentation links in proxied HTML (use carefully)
  • Legacy app migration — swap old domain strings in responses during a cutover

Tip

Set newvalue to the hostname and path your clients actually use (http://mirror.internal:8080/...), not 0.0.0.0.

docs.title: Reverse proxy
docs.text: Forward HTTP and HTTPS requests from clients to remote services. ProxyCraft rewrites paths, preserves headers, and normalizes response Content-Length automatically.

docs.title: Basic HTTPS upstream
docs.text:
{
  "prefix": "/posts",
  "match": "/posts/**",
  "backends": {
    "https": {
      "url": "https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts"
    }
  },
  "upstream": {
    "proxy": {
      "enabled": true,
      "timeout_seconds": 30
    }
  }
}

A request to GET /posts/1 is sent to https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts/1.

docs.title: Path prefix stripping
docs.text:
The prefix value is removed before the request hits the backend. Use this when your public URL layout differs from the upstream API:

Client requests Upstream receives /api/users/42 with prefix: "/api" /users/42 appended to backend base URL

docs.title: Streaming mode
docs.text:
For large or long-lived responses, set mode: "stream" on the HTTPS backend:

"https": {
  "url": "https://httpbun.com",
  "ssl": true,
  "mode": "stream"
}

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Expose an internal or third-party API on your own host and port
  • Add a single entry point in front of microservices
  • Terminate TLS at ProxyCraft and speak plain HTTP to legacy backends behind your network

See API gateway for a full walkthrough.

docs.title: Path routing
docs.text: ProxyCraft selects an endpoint for each request using Ant-style path patterns and optional weights.

docs.title: Match patterns
docs.text:
Pattern Matches /** Everything under the root /api/** Anything under /api /users/{id} /users/42, /users/alice /files/*.json /files/config.json

Patterns use the same syntax as Spring's Ant path matcher.

docs.title: Weighted selection
docs.text:
When several endpoints could match, the one with the highest weight wins:

[
  {
    "prefix": "/",
    "match": "**/*",
    "weight": 0,
    "backends": { "https": { "url": "https://fallback.example.com" } }
  },
  {
    "prefix": "/v2",
    "match": "/v2/**",
    "weight": 100,
    "backends": { "https": { "url": "https://api-v2.example.com" } }
  }
]

Traffic to /v2/users uses the v2 backend; everything else goes to the fallback.

docs.title: Identifiers for virtual upstreams
docs.text:
Give endpoints an identifier when other endpoints need to reference them:

{
  "identifier": "pypi-remote-official",
  "prefix": "/pypi-remote-official",
  "match": "/pypi-remote-official/**",
  "backends": { "https": { "url": "https://pypi.org/simple" } }
}

Identifiers are required for virtual upstream sources lists.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Route /pypi/** to a package mirror and /api/** to your application API on one port
  • Pin a high-priority rule for admin paths while keeping a catch-all for public traffic
  • Version APIs with /v1/** and /v2/** on the same proxy instance

docs.title: Security filtering
docs.text: Control who can reach your proxy with IP and User-Agent filters. Rules use Ant-style patterns and apply globally through middlewares.security.

docs.title: IP filter
docs.text:
Block or allow clients by IP address or CIDR-style patterns:

"middlewares": {
  "security": {
    "ip_filter": {
      "enabled": true,
      "blacklist": ["*.0.0.2", "203.0.113.0/24"]
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Bot filter
docs.text:
Match crawlers and scrapers by User-Agent string:

"bot_filter": {
  "enabled": true,
  "blacklist": [
    {
      "name": "googlebot",
      "user-agent": "*googlebot*"
    }
  ],
  "whitelist": []
}

Use whitelist to explicitly allow agents that would otherwise match a blacklist rule.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Internal package mirror — allow only your CI subnet and office IP ranges
  • Public API gateway — block known bad bots while keeping browsers and approved tools
  • Staging environment — restrict access before go-live

Note

Inbound authentication (Digest, NTLM, Kerberos) is on the roadmap. Today, filtering is IP- and User-Agent-based.

docs.title: Virtual upstream
docs.text: Expose one URL that tries several backing endpoints in order until one succeeds.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
{
  "prefix": "/pypi-virtual-all",
  "match": "/pypi-virtual-all/**",
  "upstream": {
    "virtual": {
      "sources": ["pypi-demo-local", "pypi-remote-official"],
      "strategy": "first-match"
    }
  }
}

sources lists identifier values from other endpoints. With first-match, ProxyCraft tries each source internally; the first response with HTTP 200 wins.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. Client requests /pypi-virtual-all/some-package/
  2. ProxyCraft tries pypi-demo-local first (e.g. files on disk)
  3. If that returns non-200, it tries pypi-remote-official (remote PyPI mirror)
  4. The winning response is returned to the client

No client-side fallback logic is required.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Hybrid registry — serve vendored packages locally, pull anything else from upstream
  • Gradual migration — keep a legacy endpoint as first source while a new backend warms up
  • Resilience — prefer a fast internal cache endpoint before a slower remote mirror

See Local and remote aggregation for a PyPI example.

docs.title: API gateway
docs.text: Put one stable URL in front of third-party or internal HTTP APIs. ProxyCraft handles routing, timeouts, and optional caching without application code.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: Your frontend or partner integrations need a fixed base URL, but backends live on different hosts, paths, or TLS setups. You want path-based routing and consistent timeouts without deploying a full API management suite.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text: Define one endpoint per upstream API. Clients only talk to ProxyCraft.

docs.title: Single upstream
docs.text:
{
  "version": "1.0",
  "name": "API gateway",
  "endpoints": [
    {
      "prefix": "/github",
      "match": "/github/**",
      "backends": {
        "https": { "url": "https://api.github.com", "ssl": true }
      },
      "upstream": { "proxy": { "enabled": true, "timeout_seconds": 30 } },
      "transformers": {
        "response": {
          "enabled": true,
          "textReplacements": [
            {
              "oldvalue": "https://api.github.com",
              "newvalue": "https://gateway.example.com/github"
            }
          ]
        }
      }
    },
    {
      "prefix": "/weather",
      "match": "/weather/**",
      "backends": {
        "https": { "url": "https://api.weather.example.com/v2" }
      },
      "upstream": { "proxy": { "enabled": true } }
    }
  ]
}
Public URL Upstream https://gateway.example.com/github/repos/... GitHub REST API https://gateway.example.com/weather/... Weather API v2

docs.title: Multiple services on one port
docs.text:
Use path routing weights to keep a catch-all while giving specific paths higher priority:

{ "prefix": "/admin", "match": "/admin/**", "weight": 100, "backends": { ... } },
{ "prefix": "/", "match": "**/*", "weight": 0, "backends": { ... } }

docs.title: TLS termination
docs.text:
Terminate HTTPS at ProxyCraft and forward to HTTP backends inside your VPC:

{
  "ssl": true,
  "server": {
    "type": "hypercorn",
    "port": 443,
    "certfile": "/etc/ssl/gateway.crt",
    "keyfile": "/etc/ssl/gateway.key"
  }
}

docs.title: When this fits
docs.text:
• BFF (backend-for-frontend) layer in front of a few REST services
  • Partner-facing facade with one DNS name
  • Gradual cutover — swap url in config instead of redeploying clients

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Reverse proxy
  • Security filtering

docs.title: Mock API for development
docs.text: Ship frontend and integration tests before the real backend exists. ProxyCraft's mock backend returns JSON from path templates with no upstream server.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: The UI team needs /users and /users/{id} responses today. The API team will not have endpoints ready until next sprint. Spinning up a separate mock server adds another deployment to maintain.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
Add a mock endpoint next to your real API routes in the same proxy.json:

{
  "identifier": "mock",
  "prefix": "/mock",
  "match": "/mock/**",
  "backends": {
    "mock": {
      "enabled": true,
      "path_templates": {
        "/users": {
          "status_code": 200,
          "content_type": "application/json",
          "body": {
            "users": [
              { "id": 1, "name": "John Doe" },
              { "id": 2, "name": "Jane Smith" }
            ]
          }
        },
        "/users/{id}": {
          "status_code": 200,
          "content_type": "application/json",
          "body": {
            "id": "${path.id}",
            "name": "User ${path.id}",
            "email": "user${path.id}@example.com"
          }
        }
      },
      "default_response": {
        "status_code": 404,
        "body": { "error": "Resource not found" }
      }
    }
  },
  "upstream": { "proxy": { "enabled": true } }
}

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
curl http://localhost:8091/mock/users
curl http://localhost:8091/mock/users/42
curl http://localhost:8091/mock/unknown   # returns 404 default

docs.title: Path variables
docs.text: Use ${path.id} (and similar) in the body to echo path segments from the template /users/{id}.

docs.title: Swap to the real API later
docs.text: When the backend is ready, add a new endpoint with a higher weight or change the frontend base path from /mock to /api. The mock config can stay for tests.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Backends
  • Echo backend — inspect raw requests during client debugging

docs.title: Package registry mirror
docs.text: Run PyPI, npm, Maven, GitHub, or Alpine package traffic through a single on-prem proxy. Builds stay fast, outbound bandwidth drops, and you control what gets cached.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: CI machines and developer laptops repeatedly download the same packages from the public internet. Registries rate-limit, links in index pages point at the official host, and air-gapped sites cannot reach upstream at all.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
ProxyCraft ships ready-made endpoint presets (see default.json in the repository) that:

  1. Proxy requests to the official registry
  2. Cache GET responses on disk
  3. Rewrite URLs in index pages so clients stay on your mirror

docs.title: PyPI mirror
docs.text:
{
  "identifier": "pypi-remote-official",
  "prefix": "/pypi-remote-official",
  "match": "/pypi-remote-official/**",
  "backends": [{
    "https": [{
      "id": "pypi-primary",
      "url": "https://pypi.org/simple",
      "weight": 10,
      "ssl": true
    }]
  }],
  "upstream": {
    "proxy": { "enabled": true, "timeout_seconds": 60 },
    "cache": {
      "file": {
        "enabled": true,
        "path": ".cache/pypi/pypi-remote-official",
        "ttl": 43200,
        "max_size_mb": 256
      }
    }
  },
  "transformers": {
    "response": {
      "enabled": true,
      "textReplacements": [
        {
          "oldvalue": "https://pypi.org/simple",
          "newvalue": "http://mirror.internal:8080/pypi-remote-official"
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}

Point pip at your mirror:

pip install requests --index-url http://mirror.internal:8080/pypi-remote-official/simple

docs.title: npm mirror
docs.text:
Same pattern with https://registry.npmjs.org as the upstream and replacements pointing at /npm-remote-npmjs.

npm config set registry http://mirror.internal:8080/npm-remote-npmjs/

docs.title: Maven mirror
docs.text: Proxy https://repo1.maven.org/maven2 under /maven-remote-central with file cache enabled. Configure Maven settings.xml mirrorOf central to your ProxyCraft URL.

docs.title: GitHub API cache
docs.text: Use /github-api to gateway https://api.github.com — helpful when many runners share one egress IP and hit rate limits.

docs.title: Alpine packages
docs.text: The /alpine-remote-official preset proxies https://dl-cdn.alpinelinux.org/alpine for APK-based images and builders.

docs.title: Production checklist
docs.text:
• Replace mirror.internal:8080 with your real hostname in all textReplacements
  • Mount .cache/ on persistent storage in Docker or Kubernetes
  • Enable IP filtering so only build farms can reach the mirror
  • Set ttl and max_size_mb to match how often packages update in your environment

docs.title: Local and remote aggregation
docs.text: Serve packages from disk when you have them; otherwise fetch from a remote registry automatically. One URL for clients, no custom fallback code.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: You vendor some Python wheels internally but still need PyPI for everything else. Maintaining two index URLs in pip.conf is error-prone. You want local first, remote second transparently.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
Use virtual upstream with first-match:

[
  {
    "identifier": "pypi-demo-local",
    "prefix": "/pypi-demo-local",
    "match": "/pypi-demo-local/**",
    "upstream": {
      "file": {
        "enabled": true,
        "path": ".files/pypi/pypi-demo-local"
      }
    }
  },
  {
    "identifier": "pypi-remote-official",
    "prefix": "/pypi-remote-official",
    "match": "/pypi-remote-official/**",
    "backends": [{
      "https": [{ "url": "https://pypi.org/simple", "ssl": true }]
    }],
    "upstream": {
      "proxy": { "enabled": true },
      "cache": { "file": { "enabled": true, "path": ".cache/pypi" } }
    }
  },
  {
    "prefix": "/pypi-virtual-all",
    "match": "/pypi-virtual-all/**",
    "upstream": {
      "virtual": {
        "sources": ["pypi-demo-local", "pypi-remote-official"],
        "strategy": "first-match"
      }
    }
  }
]

docs.title: Client configuration
docs.text:
Point pip at the virtual endpoint only:

pip install my-internal-package --index-url http://mirror.internal:8080/pypi-virtual-all/simple

docs.title: Request flow
docs.text:
pip → /pypi-virtual-all/my-package/
        ├─ try pypi-demo-local  → 200? return
        └─ else pypi-remote-official  → return (and cache)

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Approved packages on disk, everything else from upstream
  • Staging a migration from remote-only to fully local
  • Reducing bandwidth — hot packages never leave the LAN after the first remote fetch populates cache
